steps.title: Validate a fixed classroom experiment
steps.explanation: The host accepts one of four fixed experiments. The browser cannot supply arbitrary model strings, paths, settings objects or executable callbacks.

steps.title: Prepare a private project and settings home
steps.explanation: Each scenario owns its classroom files and private SDK home. Fresh runs reset only those experimental settings files, never normal user configuration.
steps.narration: Step two. Each scenario owns its classroom files and private SDK home. Fresh runs reset only those experimental settings files, never normal user configuration. The source label identifies the corresponding application statements.

steps.title: Build a typed asynchronous prompt stream
steps.explanation: The generator yields a first user message and holds the next. The displayed normal read-task branch omits the plan-to-act prompt choice and cancellation check.

steps.title: Start one live Query object
steps.code: const session = query({ prompt: prompts(), options });
steps.explanation: Keep the Query object returned by query. The SDK owns model/tool orchestration, while the host applies controls between completed prompts.

steps.title: Wait for the student’s Continue action
steps.code:
activeGate = { runId, release };
// The host awaits this gate after the first result.
steps.explanation: The first result pauses the host. Only a matching active run ID can release its gate through the Continue endpoint. The web button is an actual classroom approval action; tests automate it explicitly.
steps.narration: Step six. The first result pauses the host. Only a matching active run ID can release its gate through the Continue endpoint. The web button is an actual classroom approval action; tests automate it explicitly. The source label identifies the corresponding application statements.

steps.title: Switch the model and permission mode
steps.explanation: For the model-switch experiment, await both real methods before prompt two. The plan-to-act branch uses only the permission-mode setter, and its file guard remains active.
steps.narration: Step seven. For the model-switch experiment, await both real methods before prompt two. The plan-to-act branch uses only the permission-mode setter, and its file guard remains active. The source label identifies the corresponding application statements.

steps.title: Apply settings-file keys at runtime
steps.explanation: Use effortLevel, the settings-file key, instead of the query option effort. The acknowledged method changes this session; hooks on the next task verify the active effort.

steps.title: Persist local and user settings deliberately
steps.explanation: The real SDK writer persists supported keys to private classroom files. Local output style applies on the next request; the user effort default does not change the current live session.

steps.title: Release prompt two after acknowledgements
steps.explanation: The host awaits every selected method before releasing the second user message. A rejected change prevents that release and remains a failure.

steps.title: Verify the actual file after the live query
steps.explanation: Read the real status file after closing the live query. A model claim or Edit request is not proof that the classroom change happened.

steps.title: Load persisted settings in a fresh query
steps.explanation: The verification query omits an effort override and uses the same private settings files. Its new session has actual style/effort evidence distinct from the two live turns.
